description:
Repro (base binary):
    def effect(tag), do: (send(self(), tag); tag)
    def flush(seen) do
      receive do
        tag -> flush([tag | seen])
      after
        0 -> Enum.reverse(seen)
      end
    end
    def main(), do: dbg({effect(:sent), flush([])})
interp prints {:sent, [:sent]} (Elixir's answer); run prints {:sent, []}, so flush ran before effect. The same order difference shows through `if` plus flush. Done when: an oracle fixture with effects in each tuple element (and, to check the rule holds, list elements and call arguments) agrees on all three paths.
title: The JIT evaluates a tuple's elements left to right
